subject: history_social
passage: In the late 900s and early 1000s, merchants in Sichuan, a region in southwestern China, used coins made of iron rather than copper. Iron coins were worth little, so a large purchase required a heavy load of them; the coins needed to buy a single bolt of silk could weigh many kilograms. Merchants began leaving their coins with trusted shops in exchange for paper receipts, which they could pass to one another in place of the coins. Given these circumstances, the receipts most likely appealed to merchants because they ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: allowed merchants to buy silk without paying for it.
choices.B: were made of a material more valuable than iron.
choices.C: spared merchants from carrying heavy loads of coins.
choices.D: were accepted in every region of China, unlike coins.

explanation.why: The problem the text describes is weight: iron coins were worth so little that large purchases required many kilograms of them. A paper receipt that stood in for those coins solved that problem, since merchants could trade the receipt instead of hauling the coins.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The receipts represented coins that had been deposited, so merchants were still paying.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The receipts were valuable because they stood for stored coins, not because paper was worth more than iron.
explanation.C: Correct. Passing a light paper receipt in place of the coins avoided the burden of moving heavy iron.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text discusses only Sichuan and never says the receipts were accepted throughout China.
